reading.body:
TransCelerate, an alliance of drugmakers, runs a pharmacovigilance automation initiative that surveys its members and publishes shared tools covering AI, robotic process automation and natural language processing.

The pattern is pre-competitive collaboration on the unglamorous layer of safety work. Rather than each company validating its own automation in isolation, members pool survey findings and practical tools across safety processes. That matters for AI because validation is the slow step in deploying models in regulated work, and a framework several sponsors already accept is easier to defend to an inspector than one built alone.

The practical instruction is to reuse these frameworks rather than invent your own. The data covers the initiative's existence, its survey method, and the three technology categories it addresses. It does not give adoption numbers, named member companies, specific tools, or any regulatory decision, so it cannot tell you how far automation has actually spread or what any regulator has accepted.

terms.line: The field covering machine understanding and generation of human language. Its problems, translation, sentiment, summarization, were separate research tracks until large language models absorbed most of them into one capability.
The field of computer science dedicated to creating systems that perform tasks typically requiring human intelligence: understanding language, recognizing patterns, making decisions.

The subset of AI focused on systems that learn from data and improve with experience rather than following explicitly programmed rules. Nearly everything called AI in production is machine learning underneath.

explainer:
TransCelerate BioPharma is a nonprofit formed by biopharmaceutical companies to solve shared problems in research and development. Its intelligent automation in pharmacovigilance initiative studies how member companies use automation, machine learning and natural language processing in safety work, and publishes practical frameworks for applying and validating them.

The value of shared frameworks is efficiency and credibility. Each company does not have to invent its own approach to validating an AI tool in a GxP process, and inspectors see consistent, industry recognised methods. Companies can adapt the frameworks to their own systems while keeping the core approach.
